hook.text: Voyager 1 sends data from 15 billion miles away at 160 bits per second. Every bit is precious and near-perfect.

buildup.text: Deep-space links operate at extremely low SNR. Codes must extract every last bit of capacity from the channel.

discovery.text: NASA uses codes that operate within 1 dB of Shannon's limit. The math from 1948 guides spacecraft in 2025.

twist.text: At Shannon's limit, complexity explodes. Practical codes balance performance against decoding speed and power.

climax.text: The gap between theory and practice shrinks every decade. Shannon's limit remains the ultimate benchmark.

punchline.text: Fifteen billion miles. Every bit accounted for.

quiz.question: How close do modern deep-space codes get to Shannon's limit?
